title: Web_intelligence
summary:
The term web intelligence was coined in a paper written by Ning Zhong, Jiming Liu, Yao, and Ohsuga at the Computer Software and Applications Conference in 2000. The research about web intelligence covers many fields, including data mining (in particular web mining), information retrieval, and pattern recognition.

Web intelligence constitutes the usage of the World Wide Web as a phenomenon of retrieving information from data storage in an intelligent, efficient manner. It is a well-known research area which converges subjects such as artificial intelligence, databases, Web science, Semantic Web, and information retrieval.

Web Intelligence, also known as WebI, is a term used to represent a range of research fields and technologies jointly aiming to foster the creation of intelligent tools for web data analysis, interactions, and applications. In essence, it enables transforming raw web data into meaningful, actionable insights, which can then be used to improve business processes and decision-making.

The term is used in both academic and research contexts, focusing on AI and semantic web technologies, and in business and industry contexts, focusing on business intelligence and reporting tools. WEBINT, or Web Intelligence, is also used as a general term referring to relevant and valuable data collected from the internet that has been processed and channeled towards a particular objective.
